Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. It's here. It is here. The number on the map is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 13 or 30, the interpreter could not hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the very same place. Now we are going to see a hole here to the right where a shell fell. There's another one that's even bigger. A young photographer from Dubrovnik got killed there. His name is Pavo Urban. I think this is a young man of 19 or 20. He was studying photography, and unfortunately, this was the last picture he took here in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, did you actually witness the death of Pavo Urban with your eyes?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: No. Later on I saw photographs, and I heard what his mother had to say. She lives there in the neighbourhood, so she saw her son being killed with her very own eyes. A man ran up to him, but unfortunately he could no longer be helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So -- but what you're telling the Trial Chamber is on the basis of what people have told you, not on the basis of what you have witnessed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the footage I took, but I did not see the death of Mr. Pavo Urban myself. However, his mother spoke about this on a countless number of radio and TV programmes, and that's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move on. Before we do, perhaps you could put a little C now in the fine pen in front of you by St. Blaise Church at the point where the ordnance lay.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could turn your attention back to the monitor, we'll continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see what people look like. They look lost. You see all the shops are smashed up. Again there is this UNESCO flag, this particular sign. This is the archives of Dubrovnik. Now I'm going to move with the camera here, that it's going to show the clock, the old clock, and you will see the time, twenty minutes to twelve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And what is the significance of that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The significance? We're going to see it in the next seconds, that the town was quite empty, that people were still in shelters and that there was still an alert in town and that there is only a few people who are repairing things. There is a moment that is quite typical of Dubrovnik. We will see the shops. We will see the city bank. We're going to see the shops where there were shoes, there was jewellery there. Nobody took a thing. There was no looting. Through that we can see the culture and standard of living in Dubrovnik itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is, the UN flag on fort Minceta, the main fort. That is number 1 on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And that flag was flying on the day before, was it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, of course. Yes. Many days before that too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The cars can be seen here, the cars belonging to the local people. You can see me here. And since I did not record the date, I'm going to ask him something to that effect now, like, "What's the date today?" This is the time when this street would be crowded before the war and after the war, and now you see it quite empty at midday, and you can see the atmosphere. This is the Franciscan cloister and its church. It was hit too. It was hit from say Zarkovica, from the position of Zarkovica, straight from there. It could not have been hit from anywhere else but that position above Dubrovnik, Zarkovica. Again you can see the Red Cross here. Again it was a marked place that was being targeted. There was a place there called Domus Christus. That is where people received aid, medicines, and also the oldest pharmacy in Europe is housed there, perhaps one of the oldest pharmacies in Europe. I'm sorry. On the right-hand side you can see the bank and also a Maljutka. And it did not explode. It was there in the wall. Could you please move this arrow a bit to the right. Yeah. There it is. There was this thread-like thing hanging there, like made of nylon or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, it's not too clear from that video whether or not we can see the wire threads hanging there, but we take your word for it. Could you tell us in which geographical direction, or which geographical feature is directly opposite that hole?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The east, the east.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And what do you have in the east, geographically speaking, if you look at your map, you know the --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The letter A is in the east, and that is where we saw Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, once again I will show you later on a photograph of the cupola of that tower that you see in front of you. It's not too visible from this angle. We'll leave that for a later stage, but let's move on with your film for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If you could keep your commentary going, sir, as you see fit.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I will tell you when there is something important. I'm looking for the clock now. The clock should be up here. Yes, here it is. 11 hours, 40 minutes. It can be seen here. That is the Old City clock that has been working for centuries now. It works today as well. It shows the correct time. Listen to the text. Question: "What is the date?" Answer: "The 7th of December." So you heard a person who told me what the date was, the 7th of December, 1991. The only being that was free to roam about. Listen to the sounds. See? Everything is shattered. This is a well-known cafe and then a pharmacy next to it. People are trying to save what can be saved. This is Zudioska Street, the street of the Jews. Could you stop here for a moment. On the right-hand side is the street called Zudioska where one of the oldest synagogues in Europe is. It was hit too. Unfortunately, I did not record that, but I know it from the official information provided that it had been hit too. Can we go on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Before we do that, you talked about people protecting whatever they had. Now, we're accustomed, from the news of world events, that when tragedies take place of this nature, there is looting. Was there any looting in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: That's what I said a minute ago. You see here on the left-hand side there is a young man who is a salesman in this shop, and he put some wooden boards there. On the right-hand side is another citizen. There is not a single case of looting that was registered or any devastation whatsoever. So that is a characteristic of the citizens of Dubrovnik, that they would not want to steal anything that is not their own.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Dubrovnik was repaired later on, all these vaults were replaced by new ones because they were all destroyed. We will see later on, on a facade, how stone was actually melting because of the extreme heat. So all of this had to be redone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, you --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is a street where a young man was killed. This young man got killed. There was a shop there called Mediator. He was killed by a shrapnel that hit him straight in the heart. I think he was 18 or 19 years old. It was back in this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Once again, sir, could you name that street? If you can't name it --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It is the street of Miha Pracata, I think, and the young man's name is Skocko, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, please with your fine blue pen, if you could mark with the letter D the street as you are turning off the Stradun. Just put a D on the corner of the Stradun and that particular street.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is where he was killed, in this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same story all over again. People are putting these wooden boards up. This is Palmoticeva Street. I used to live in that street before, and on the corner there is a bank, you see, and nobody's touched the bank. There is no one at the bank. Like in any bank, there would have to be lots of money there. So the same old story repeating itself yet again. Now we're going to reach the festival building, the building of the Dubrovnik Festival. You see, there is no one there. Zarkovica is up there. It can be seen from here. You see? Not only the main street, all the streets were targeted and destroyed. There's a cosmetics shop here, and then there is a street with cafes, well known in Dubrovnik. This is a street that I was born in, by the way. This is the street called Siroka. An extremely valuable building was hit there. Not a mere building, a palace. When we get closer to it, you will see what it's like and then you will be able to appreciate the value and the antiquity of the building. You will see all the debris and the extent of devastation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: You talk about a palace, an extremely special palace being hit on that day in this particular street. Do you know the exact address of that palace? If you don't, perhaps you could mark it on the map with the next letter in the alphabet we've reached, which I believe is the letter E.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Very well. Here it is exactly. I'm going to reach it on the other side with the camera, so you'll see. A Dubrovnik artist, Ivo Grbic, was there or, rather, his studio was there, and overnight he lost everything; his paintings, his equipment, his house, everything. He and his sister remained homeless overnight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this house the famous Dubrovnik poet, author and writer was born. Ivo Vojinovic is his name. He lived for a long time in Dubrovnik but he also lived in Belgrade and his works have been performed and as he is a great author will continue to be performed worldwide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Was his house struck on the 6th of December, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is the 6th. Yes. Everything that we are looking at was hit the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And what's the exact address of this house?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: From this junction here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Could it be marked with the letter F so that we keep a record of this. A tiny little letter F.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "a tiny little letter F"? A small one, a handwritten F?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, because we don't want any confusion at a later date. I might have missed a letter out. If I have --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I remember vividly and all the memories are coming back to me. I cannot make a mistake even if I were to repeat the same story a hundred times all over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I might have missed a letter out. If I have, the transcript will reflect the record anyway. So if we're marking this particular building with a letter F, then that will stand out on the record. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Awhile ago, I was at the archives. Then I moved my camera towards this yellow portion, and I asked one observer, I believe that he was a Belgian or a French, what this yellow was, and he said that these were probably incendiary phosphorous bombs. He used the word "phosphorous." I remember that with precision. The intention being for it to set ablaze whatever -- the place where it fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So with your pen once again, please mark on -- where you saw that staining with the letter G. The letter G, please.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm crossing the street so that I can record the festival palace. This is it, the festival palace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Its exact address, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The street's name is Od Sigurate. What letter should I put there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The letter H.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: So the summer festival has been held for 54 years, and it epitomises all the wit and art that has passed through Dubrovnik with Herbert von Karajan, Sergio Perticaroli, up to Sir Lawrence Olivier, the greatest artists of our times over the last 54 years, rather. So this is where the offices were, the official reception rooms. In this section there were some administrative units and in the attic was the archive. So this is a house that was almost completely demolished as the bare walls still hand, as we will be able to see a bit better a bit later. And for Dubrovnik, this was something totally incomprehensible. No one in Dubrovnik could be convinced that this was not deliberate, not intentional, that it was precisely with intent that this building was targeted in order to destroy the history of the festival. And here to the left you have the Franciscan cloister, and as you can see on the footage, it -- that building has a rich archive, and they were also hit on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, what actually happened to the archives themselves?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The archive was completely destroyed. It is a pity that we hadn't microfilmed the content of the archives. It was a unique archives, and later the director of the festival called upon the citizens who had -- who had anything, who had gone to concerts and performances and had saved at home their programmes of these concerts, to bring those in, and in this way we managed to salvage some of the documentation, but it was really a pitiful, wretched end to it, to the archives. This was the destruction of a very beautiful period in the history of the Dubrovnik Festival.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, it seems that you're fairly well acquainted with this building. Is there any particular reason why? If so, perhaps you could enlighten us as to the architectural and historic features of this building.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This was a palace. Obviously this building, inside it was all in paintings and frescos. On the floors there were wonderful, beautiful Italian tiles hundreds of years old. In fact, even as a child and later as a recognised and renowned artist, I performed at the Dubrovnik Festival. I had my solo concerts, and I had a large musical of mine staged at the palace. This musical was also performed in one of the best renowned theatres in Belgrade, the Terazije in Belgrade. And this is a performance that toured the whole world: Warsaw, Moscow, Leningrad, Split, and as I already said, in Belgrade. At that time it was also -- no, it was also performed at the Dubrovnik summer festival I believe in 1988 so that I have very deep feelings about this building and I am very familiar with it. As I said, it had beautiful architecture and generally it was beautiful. And downstairs there was a cafe. There was a place, a gathering place where artists came, and you could meet the greatest world renowned artists who would drop in there to have coffee or tea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see that this woman just cannot make up her mind to run across the street to the other side. And here you can see how the stone melted. And this is a family house. You can see the coat of arms. This is a family house, and every family house, 500, 600 years old had a coat of arms of the family. And a bit later, down here, you will see how the extreme temperature made the stone melt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, the particular address of that building with the coat of arms, do you know it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It is also Od Sigurate Street, but on the other side here is the Festival Palace, and this is this building. Shall I mark it with a letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, please. The letter I we've reached. Tiny little letter I.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it is also empty and all burnt. You can see the molten stone here. If I may, you can see the people scurrying, running across the street. It is still very unsafe. So these people who I met, these are my acquaintances and friends in Dubrovnik. We more or less all know each Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. other. These are people 20 years old or so, so it would have been logical for them to be members of an army, but these were people who normally lived in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, please look at the cupola there. That building, that monument is what exactly?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the cupola which we saw a minute ago. This is the bell tower of the cloister, the Franciscan cloister, and the shell came in from the direction of Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And, sir, that is normal, is it, this area that I'm pointing to now with the arrow, or is it some abnormal feature on the cupola? Is it damaged?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: No. The cupola is damaged. There is a hole on it. You will see perhaps later in the next clip this is of course not normal. And you have the gromobran also damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Well, we will see -- is this what you're referring to, the lightning conductor?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: We're still on the Stradun, sir, when we look at this?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: As you can see, there is funny sides to it as well. This was a proud lad out of some pride and protest. He sat on his bike to drive through the main street of Dubrovnik on it. Otherwise, this is not a street which allowed motorists, bikers in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Are you able to name this particular street, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The name of this street is Djordjo -- no. It's Cubranoviceva, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So with a little J, please mark that.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now proceeding down this street that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now we shall reach the Od Puca Street. Just look at the devastation. So this is the mansion, the palace in which this artist Grbic lived. It has been repaired but it can never be restored to its original state. Of course you can see by the balconies what a wonderful building this had been. I'm saying this because I really can't see for what reason fire was opened at this particular building. Because there was this artist painter who lived in it. There was no reason whatsoever for it to be demolished and for this man to be killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at this balcony. It has wrought iron latticework. You can see this part where there is still a smouldering fire. We will see the fire, in fact, in a minute. Yes. It is still smouldering. In fact, parts of it are in flames. The balcony on the other side of the street. This is Siroka Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, I don't believe we've actually marked Mr. Grbic's apartment or palace. Perhaps you could with a letter K show us where that was.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: If you allow me to observe, we've already marked it with an E.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Awhile ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this actually can demonstrate how much the people were humiliated, degraded. There's -- there was nothing to be bought. There was no food. There was no water. You could have millions of dollars in your pockets, all these shops had been devastated, there was nothing to be had. Let's go on, please. There's a very interesting scene very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: This particular address that we've stopped at at the moment, are you aware of where that is, the address of it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It is the Od Puca Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Do you have a number, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I'll show you on the map. If I could be provided with a map, please. And should I mark it with some letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Maybe the letter K I think we've reached. Is it K or J? Use the letter K, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [In English] K, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. You can see here on the upper storey there was a concert piano. What remained is only its carcass, the iron carcass of a large concert piano. This is St. Joseph Church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Was St. Joseph Church hit, sir, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Here above the door there is a small, perhaps half-metre, sculpture and its head was hit off, and here it says the inscription St. Joseph will make it up to you a hundredfold -- or may he make it up to you a hundredfold, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is yet another palace, huge building, and we shall also see its coat of arms when we move on. It was totally burnt to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The address of that palace, sir, do you know it?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the Od Puca Street. The adjacent street, what letter shall I put here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The letter L, I believe we've reached, yes.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I have put it, the letter L.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Do you know the number of that particular address on Od Puca Street, as you say?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this corner where these houses -- where the house burnt and the walls fell down, and there probably was no number on the house because I would have recorded it, but I have placed the letter L on exactly the right spot where the building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: This is the same palace that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same one. The same one. That is why I'm not saying anything more. It so happens that this woman remained -- escaped with her life in the first half of the house. On to the left there is a large church which was also hit. It is in the centre of town. It had never been devastated before. My friends used to come there and came there to practice their religions. In contrast to that, everything vis-a-vis this house was burnt to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: This particular monument, do you know its name? You say it's a church.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It is the Orthodox church. That is how we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, we've been seeing a lot of damage so far, sir, and it is noticeable that in a number of the images that we have seen, that the roofs are missing. Do you have an explanation for why the roofs are missing?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Because the shell landed obviously on the roof, and everything caved in and was set on fire. The shells came from air, not from the ground.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you can see the cross up there on Srdj, the wings of which, so to speak, have already fallen off so that a new cross had to be erected later. And here we see the pillar, the column of the funicular which was also in existence before but was demolished in this attack on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The 5th, the interpreter believes the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the support, the pillar of the cross which is a sign of protection of Dubrovnik, and it overlooks the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: You see the pillar, the support part. What happened to the cross part? Are you aware? If you aren't, just say you're not and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: They were shelled from ships, and later they would take it out completely. I believe it was a matter of prestige which particular ship would actually hit it, and it was fired from the sea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Is that on the basis of what you heard, sir, or what you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Later there was some TV programmes that were prepared by journalists much more famous than I myself saying that the shells were landing from the southern side under the cross and from the direction of the south the only shells could have come if they were fired from the vessels.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: That's the conclusion of the journalists. Let's just move on, shall we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Tell us the street we're continuing down now, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: We're still in Od Puca Street. Across, the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, please mark on the map the letter -- the next letter. I believe it -- is it letter M? M, M for mother. If you could mark on the map where the Serb Orthodox church is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I have. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly opposite the church. I can see that these are palaces by their architecture. There used to be a coat of arms, probably of the family which owned it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop for a minute there. This is where a very renown gentleman from Dubrovnik had a shop, and this was a shop owned by a Serb. And I say the Serb's boutique, the Serb's shop. This only shows that people of all ethnic backgrounds and religions lived normally in Dubrovnik, that they had mutual respect irrespective of their political or religious affiliations. This is why I say the Butega od Srbina, the Serb's boutique. This was only normal then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He actually made picture frames, painting frames, and sold them in the shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: What are you saying there, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the street of Miha Pracata, but we call it the Music School Street because there is a music school in that street. So that is why we tend to call it that way, the Music School Street. This is the mosque of Dubrovnik, this door right over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Please, sir, with a letter N, mark the mosque of Dubrovnik. N.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a palace too. We're going to see the coat of arms, now. We're going to see the family coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And this is on Miha Pracata?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of that is there. That is the street of Miha Pracata, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And are you aware of the exact address with the number of this particular palace that we're about to see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is vis-a-vis the letter N.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see the coat of arms here, the family coat of arms. This is the family coat of arms. I don't want to refer to the family name lest I make a mistake but this is a palace that belonged to an old family of Dubrovnik. This is very similar to the festival building. This is what the festival building was like too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And are you continuing --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Would you stop here for a moment? This is where the young man was killed. That's the shop. That's where the arrow is, that's where the door is, actually. The shop sign, Discont Mediator. That is where he got killed. The shooting was on this side, but then something ricochetted and that's how he got killed. See, this was a palace too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "on this side," what do you mean by "on this side"?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I mean this side. The shooting came from my left-hand side. That's the east. That's where the east is. So the shell fell somewhere around here and it ricochetted. So it was not a direct hit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Church of St. Joseph. St. Joseph is headless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: You've already marked that on the map, sir, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I do believe you did earlier when you were talking about the charity box, but maybe I'm mistaken. In that case, perhaps you could mark it with the letter O.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the house where piano is, the letter K, and then L is the palace, and then the Church of St. Joseph is between the two. So what should I put between here now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I believe we've reached the letter O, small little letter O.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: O, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, that is St. Joseph, is it, carrying the baby Jesus?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right, but he is headless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Do you know when he became headless, when he was decapitated?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: On the previous day. On the previous day, on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The street being Ulica --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Cubranoviceva.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And this street, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the festival building vis-a-vis. This is Cubranoviceva then. This is Cubranoviceva, again near the festival building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, what do we see here? Look where the arrow is pointing.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: We see that there is no roof. We see that there used to be a roof but that there is no roof there any longer. We also see smoke coming from that void, so we see that it had just been devastated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Are you able to name that building, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The Dubrovnik Festival.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the festival building again. This is the Franciscan cloister. This is where the Red Cross signs are, when somebody needed medicine or any kind of assistance, and this is the oldest pharmacy in Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, we're drawing to the close of your video now, but did you witness any damage in the cloister itself on that day? Will we see any of that damage on this video film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, you saw some palm trees there, but here inside you can see the dining-room of the Franciscan monks. Pater Polonio -- Mato Polonio. That was his name. He was my personal friend. Now we're going to see where the shell fell in the dining-room. There are vast archives there of Gundulic, Marin Drzic, the great poets of Dubrovnik. This is Pater Polonio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And what happened to the archives of those great poets?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: You can hear the siren now sounding off the end of the state of alert. So I was filming all of this while there was still a state of alert, while it was still dangerous. And this shell could have fallen only from the side of Zarkovica and Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Old furniture, centuries old. We'll also see other damage that was done. See?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, please take --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to something else. There was a lot more footage that was taken, but this is an abbreviated version. So I would like the Honourable Trial Chamber to know that, if necessary, we have more material, but I believe that this speaks sufficiently about what happened on the 7th of December, 1991, in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, once again have a look at the damage that the arrow is pointing to at the moment.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is a part of this priceless object, 200 years old. There are Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. no stonesmiths like that left. Nobody can make that kind of thing nowadays. This is a history of a people, of a nation. And also the archives, the great archives were there. This is where the works of Sorkocevic are, a great composer from Dubrovnik. And also the texts of Marin Drzic, and Gundulic's famous texts, Osman, Dubravka. This is where I wrote my musical called Dundo Maroje because they let me use the premises. In a way my own soul is there, so this involved such hurt, such humiliation. I cannot understand until the present day why all of this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, put yourself up there with your back facing the wall, standing where that damage is, if you look at the arrow. You're now looking out in front of you. In which geographical direction are you looking? What do you see, if possible?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side is the east, here, right here. This is the view from Zarkovica or Bosanka precisely, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, all the damage that we've been viewing up until now, did Dubrovnik, the Old Town of Dubrovnik, look like this on the 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the guardian of the monastery. This is the flag. If it was there, obviously overnight it fell too. You see how much of the wall is missing. This is the interior of the monastery, where the walls were broken through. The shells fell in through there. On the walls there are pictures of the great men of Dubrovnik, well-known people from the history of Dubrovnik. This is certainly a councilman from Old Dubrovnik. Then there are also pictures of Rudjer Boskovic, Getaldic, and other great artists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you for that. We have perhaps reached the end of our viewing of your video. We will submit the video to the Trial Chamber at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Seventh. Can I ask you whether we're going to view the footage of the 6th? Are we going to see the cause of all of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, we can do that if you wish, but perhaps for the time being we'll submit this exhibit. I have other footage which I'd like to show you later which includes footage of the 6th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must stop now because of the tape. That will be received as an exhibit, the film, and we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is something very important in relation to this film, but if you so instruct me, then I'm going to raise that immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Before the break Mr. Petrovic raised a matter, and in the spirit of collegiality, we have had an opportunity to discuss the matter. I will explore it with the witness because we are about to see another part of the witness's film. If Mr. Petrovic, of course, feels that there is still a necessity to raise the matter, I'm sure he will do so at the conclusion of the film. As I say I'm proposing now to show another three minutes of film footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, if you could please look at the video monitor in front of you. Do you see there a scene filmed --

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was taken from my balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, on which day was this taken?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: On the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: We're going to in a minute see a few more minutes of footage pursuant to your request and of course our desire to give the Court an indication of what happened on the morning of the 6th of December. Now, going through your video which is currently being played to you, we have noticed three distinct dates, month of November, where we saw the car by the walls being blown up; the 7th of December, which is where we spent most of the time discussing, showing your walk through the Old Town; and we're now about to see footage of the 6th of December. So this is a collection of footage. Who made that collection? Who did the cuts?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I filmed this from my balcony, from the balcony of my apartment, and I'm the one who did the cuts, if you can put it that way. I took out what the most important footage was, what the most important things to be seen were, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So if I can put it another way, you were the person who did the editing of this particular film that we've been seeing today.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, look, while I was waiting for things to happen, there were long pauses, so in order to avoid the viewers having to wait through, I made the cuts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, please understand I'm not criticising you. I'm just clarifying the matter for purposes of legal technicalities, if I can put it that way. Now, did anyone edit your film apart from yourself?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Only I. Only I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think that should probably clarify the matter. If Mr. Petrovic has anything more to say about it, I'm sure he will raise his objection in due course. Now, let us show this portion of the film to you. Once again, if you feel the need to comment, please do so. If I feel the need to stop and ask you to expand, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we're going to see the shells falling on the Old Town. You can hear the strong wind blowing then. This is the bura wind that is famous in Dubrovnik. We can go on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We're about to hear some noise and I didn't want you to be speaking whilst we hear the noise. The bura wind that you mentioned, which direction is that wind?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It blows from the land to the sea, but every now and then you will hear this. I think that this is stereo sound, too. You can actually hear the whizzing of the shells flying literally in front of my nose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: All right. Do you mean shells or projectiles, sir, the whizzing ones?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Projectiles. "Shells" is a general term or, rather, I don't really know this terminology, what flew there, but this is to prove that the shooting came from the east towards the town, that is to say westward.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And that is behind you, as it were.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, what time of day is this filmed, this particular portion the film we're about to see?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This was filmed in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Can you be more exact?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: On the morning of the 6th. Perhaps around 8.00 or 9.00, say. It can also be seen from the sun rays.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Let us continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you heard the shell now? Have you heard it now? Have you heard this projectile flying by?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: We can put the film back, if necessary, but maybe it is worth inquiring of the Trial Chamber whether a whizzing sound was noticed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I thank Your Honours. So may the record reflect that in fact at that portion of film, just slightly before six minutes and five seconds, a whizzing sound was heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the building of the music school that was hit now, the building of the music school on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... this building?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Exactly. A bit to the right, though. That is all the building of the music school. Where the arrow is, that's exactly where the music school building is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So we will see that later, with a plume of smoke.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'm moving the camera around, but this is the pressure from the shells that has affected me. It's the air pressure that's affected me, and it's pushing me back and that's why the camera is moving. Some of it is due to fear, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, please see the area that my arrow is now encircling. This is at seven minutes and 25 seconds. What can we see there?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Here it is. This is the music school. It was hit, yes, exactly, and you can see the plume of smoke, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I think that's fairly demonstrative of what happened, what you saw from your balcony on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: At this point in time I'd like to submit the video, the CD on which that video is contained, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before we as the Defence would be in a position to state our views on my learned friend Mr. Kaufman's proposal, there is still one thing that is unclear, and Mr. Jusic explained it only in part today. The questions are the following, Your Honour: How many films are there? What is their duration? When were all these films made? Is there an integral version? Was the integral version handed over to the Prosecution? And finally, in relation to the last explanation given by Mr. Kaufman, when did Mr. Jusic make the cuts and according to which criterion? Your Honour, those are the questions that we believe have to be dealt with before a compilation is admitted. This is obviously a compilation. We have no reason to doubt Mr. Jusic's intentions, and we're not doing that. However, in order to be in a position to present our own views in a valid manner, we need to know about all the things that I referred to just now. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I may just briefly reply. Mr. Petrovic seems to be raising two matters, one being a matter of non-disclosure of material, the other being a matter concerned with the authenticity of the video film which has been shown to the Trial Chamber. If I may deal with the second issue first. I would have thought and I would submit that the matters raised by Mr. Petrovic are or should rather be the subject of cross-examination; when the cuts were made, why they were made. These are the sort of things that can be challenged in cross-examination and do not necessarily affect the admissibility of the video which I'm currently seeking to tender to the Trial Chamber. The first issue also should not really affect the admissibility of the video which I am seeking to address and tender to the Trial Chamber. Whether or not there are further videos which Mr. Jusic has made, I can inquire with him now. What I can say is that this video which has been -- which is being tendered at the current moment in time is the only video that we have in our possession from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, the issue of non-disclosure, Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may just consult with Ms. Somers. She wants to tell me something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may repeat: Once again, with respect to the issue of non-disclosure, we have only been handed from this particular witness this particular video film, and we have handed over and disclosed that to my learned friend Mr. Petrovic. Once again, the -- in my submission, the Office of the Prosecutor is not obliged to turn over anything which it obviously has not got in its possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, can you assist me. Is this film one film which you -- from which you have edited some parts, or is this a compilation from a number of different films?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already explained how this was recorded, but when your people were there, when they talked to me in Dubrovnik, at one point in time I said that perhaps I was a bit too much of a patriot and perhaps I'm not going to say everything that should be said, but then I said I have films, and they were really taken by surprise and they said, "What kind of films?" And I said I had recordings from the 6th and the 7th and also before that, from November. That is how this happened. That is how I handed over these films to the Honourable Court. There is a longer version here, but it is also here in court. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You haven't answered what I was searching for. I didn't make my question clear, I fear. I want to know whether you had just one film in the camera when you took each one of the periods of photography - one in October or November and then one on the 6th of December and one on the 7th of December - or were there different films in the camera on those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I had two cassettes. I was not prepared for filming, so I even had to erase parts of some footage in order to be able to make this. So I was not getting prepared for war footage. I did this spontaneously. This is it. This is what I did on my own. I took the footage from my balcony. What we saw before was the 7th of December, 1991, and what we saw just now is the morning of the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have described the process by which you edited the film that you had taken. You did say that you edited out parts where you had paused for a long time. Did you edit out other material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. First of all, I do not have the facilities to do any editing at home, so I went to this plain old shop in Dubrovnik where you can rent videos. So what I did was I cut the pauses. There was no other editing, just in order to bridge this between the two pauses. None of this which we saw now taken that morning was edited. The camera was switched on and then it was switched off eventually. No cuts were made, that was it, the morning of the 6th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did I hear you say you had a longer film here with you as well as the film we have seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it here with me, my lawyers have it. At least, that's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean here in The Hague or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I may be able to enlighten the Trial Chamber as to the cause of the confusion perhaps. When Mr. Jusic came to The Hague approximately two weeks ago when he was due to give evidence, he was proofed, and for the purposes of the proofing session we showed Mr. Jusic a shortened version of the film which is now being presented to Your Honours. So it may be the case, and of course I will have to clarify this with the witness, that the witness is confusing the shortened version that was shown to him with the long version which has actually being shown in court today. It may be the case that Mr. Jusic thinks what we are showing now, which is in fact the entire footage that we received from him, is in fact the shortened version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could explore that with Mr. Jusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, do you remember being proofed in The Hague or visiting The Hague and myself and Ms. Somers approximately two weeks ago?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: That's true. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And we were preparing you for your evidence in court today?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: In fact, we were going through all the substance that I gave during my statements in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And we showed you a video film. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And we basically did the same exercise that we've been doing in court today, going through the video film, stopping it and asking you for your comments.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: And you also asked me the same thing, whether I took this, and I gave the same answer I gave here today, that I took it from my balcony by myself with my own camera on the 6th and the 7th. So it's not for me to recognise now whether it's the shorter version or the longer version. These are the important clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you under the impression that that video that we showed you -- Sir, are you under the impression that that video that we showed you when you came here approximately two weeks ago is the same video that has now been broadcast in the Trial Chamber, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Definitely it is this material, but I cannot give the exact Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. duration. It is that film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So, I think, Your Honours, at this point in time the explanation or the further clarification matter lies with the Office of the Prosecutor and not with the witness. And I can inform the Trial Chamber that the video that was shown to Mr. Jusic when he visited approximately two weeks ago was the shortened version of the video which is currently being displayed in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, do you have any submission to make on admissibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Just a moment, please. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, during the examination-in-chief of Witness Jusic, he said on several occasions, if I remember correctly, including a few minutes ago, he said that there were a few films. That is one point. The second point, Your Honour: Every one of these cassettes is individually much longer than these 30 minutes that we have on this particular tape. Where is that material? What is on that material? How was this edited, cut, put together? That is a cause of serious concern for us. So there are certainly several hours of material involved. How and according to what criterion was all of this reduced to what Your Honours had the opportunity of seeing, which is 21 minutes in one version, in the second version it is about 40 minutes, and there has to be several hours of material. That is what causes our concern. We did not know about that. We heard from Mr. Jusic's evidence today that that is the volume of material involved. So that is our concern. That is a problem as far as its admission into evidence is concerned. Of course, if we were to have insight into the entirety of this material from which this was created, this which was shown to Your Honours, then we could say, yes, that's it. But at this point in time, I don't think that that would be proper. I don't think that this document in this way is acceptable for admission. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: By your leave. The Office of the Prosecutor has in its possession two videos only from this witness. One of the videos is an edited video version of the video that has currently been displayed by the Court, and that video was edited by the Office of the Prosecutor. Both of these videos, which are contained on compact disk, have been given to the Defence. They have been timely disclosed. The first of the videos, the long version of the video which has been displayed in court today, was disclosed a long time ago. The edited version was disclosed in the run-up to Mr. Jusic's attending court today. Your Honour, I do not believe that I can add anything useful further on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I propose, Mr. Petrovic, to admit the CD containing -- or the CD version of the video into evidence. There is no issue of non-disclosure. The evidence discloses that all that is on the film was taken by this witness on the days that he indicates. The content of such a film is, therefore, relevant and of probative force for the purposes of the trial and is thereby admissible. The question of whether there is some doubt to be attached to what it contains, because certain parts have been edited out and how much has been edited out, is something that you may fully explore with the witness during cross-examination, and the effect of that may or may not alter the weight which this Chamber would otherwise attach to what is presently shown on the film, but I don't think those questions touch the issue of admissibility in this particular case. The situation is quite similar to that which you might find if there was tendered before us a film shown on a television station. There can be no question but that the photographer would have filmed a great deal more film than is shown by the television station, say, in a news programme, and this, as we have both the photographer and the editor, who is the witness, the Chamber is in a position to accept what is presently tendered as properly admissible subject to any question of weight which may be further informed by your cross-examination. So it will be received and will be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may. May I just say one sentence to clarify what my learned colleague has said. I don't want to leave this equivocal. It is true that we were disclosed two versions, but these two versions are not two cassettes or a number of cassettes that Mr. Jusic is talking about. But of course, we shall raise these questions in more detail and more specifically during our cross-examination. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, had you finished, Mr. Kaufman?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I will be concluding, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I am indeed drawing to the end of examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I just saw you sitting. I thought you had actually sat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I was trained to sit when my learned friend makes his submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, I'm going to show you some photographs now. If we can start with the first photograph, which has already been exhibited in this Court as P31. If it may be recalled. If that's a problem, I have a copy here. Mr. Jusic, you can look at the screen in front of you. There's no need to put it on the ELMO, but -- Mr. Jusic, before you answer, I'm going to be showing you a number of prominent monuments, high monuments, if I may put it that way, in the Old Town of Dubrovnik. I'd like you to tell us what those monuments are as we see them. And once again going through the procedure which may be quite familiar to you now from my earlier questioning, please try and tell us in which direction the hole that we see is facing. So here in P31 we have a photograph. What is that monument, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the bell tower with the clock which shows the full hour and half hour. It is very old. It was hit by a shell which came from the east, either from Zarkovica or the area of Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So that particular hole that we see in the photograph is facing towards Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have an objection at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing which I ask is that the witness be asked the question when was this damage sustained. To discuss the photograph, we need to know the time when the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please don't reply to me. My learned colleague will ask you that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I didn't dream for one moment not to ask that witness that question. Rest assured, that is the next question that I will be asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we can get a date, it will clear things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The reason why I'm starting off with this particular photograph, as the witness will now tell us:

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: When was this hole incurred, sir? Hopefully I'm showing things in chronological order.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: The bell tower was pierced about 3.00 in the afternoon. I was just passing by on my way home. I heard the whiz and I turned and looked and I saw the hole. So this took place in the days following the 6th or the 7th. I cannot recall the exact date, but it was after those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It could have in fact been in the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next photograph, if I may. Yes. If you could look at your video monitor.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the cathedral. What we see right now is the cupola of the Dubrovnik cathedral. This same shell or, rather, just like the previous shell, this shell hit the bell tower on one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, the date shown on this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The date shown on this particular portion of video film is the 7th of December, 1991. Can you tell us when that damage was incurred? If you can't tell us and you don't know or you're not sure, say, "I'm not sure," or, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: If it was incurred on the 7th of December, 1991, on the 7th of December, we were cleaning the town, clearing up the town, and then it started again, and perhaps it was between the 7th and the 8th, during the night. But since this is obviously daylight, it was in the afternoon of the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask you please to try not to speculate. If you don't know the date on when the damage occurred, say, "I don't know." Please don't speculate. So once again I ask you. This image was photographed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness answered the question. I don't see why he has to be asked the same question twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Carry on, Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Once again, sir, do you personally have a record of seeing that impact when it occurred? If you didn't, say you didn't. Please don't guess.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps I was inspired by this date which is inscribed on the photograph, the 7th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, going back to P31, sir, once again, if we can have P31 pulled up on the screen. The date of this damage, sir, once again I would ask you not to guess. Do you know when that damage was incurred or are you not sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I protest again. I fail to see why my learned colleague Kaufman keeps reverting twice to things which have been clarified or shall he keep reverting to this question until he gets the answer that he wishes to get? I ask you kindly to prevent this line of questioning. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer at the moment, I would see, Mr. Petrovic, is one in which the witness has indicated uncertainty, and the question being asked is whether or not he knows. So I would allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: So once again, sir, if you're not sure, say you're not sure. If you know, say you know, but please do not guess. It's important that we understand exactly what is in your knowledge. Do you know when this particular hole was caused from what you witnessed with your eyes?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm a meticulous person by nature, and I have an association of a concatenation of events in my mind in connection with this. So in order not to speculate in respect of these events, what I can say is that I cannot decidedly say this took place on such-and-such date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let us move on. I showed you a photograph. I'd now like this to be tendered. This is the cathedral that you talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I haven't asked for it formally to be tendered and assigned an exhibit number, so I will do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Am I correct, Mr. Kaufman, in understanding the evidence of Mr. Jusic to be that this damage actually occurred on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Well, I understood his last answer to be, Your Honour, that he can't speculate about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P79.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jusic, one more photograph. What's this monument?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the bell tower of the Franciscan cloister. The same position, namely it was hit from the same direction as the previous one, from the east side, from Zarkovica, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Namely, once again, which direction is the hole facing? I wouldn't ask you to draw a conclusion, just tell me, in which direction is the hole facing?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: It is facing the direction of the east, the direction of Zarkovica hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, once again, do you know when this damage was incurred? Yes or no. Once again, I ask you, if you're not sure, do not speculate, and say, "I'm not sure."

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I ask that this photograph be tendered and assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P80.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jusic, you will be pleased to know that this is in fact the last photograph I'm going to show you, and we'll go through the same exercise once again. The hole, in which direction is the hole facing?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: This is the Onofrius fountain. It is facing the same direction as in the previous photograph, the bell tower; it is facing Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: The hole is facing Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Once again, are you aware on which day the damage was caused from what you witnessed? If you are, please tell us so, if not, say"I'm not sure,""I don't know," whatever.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to assume. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, there was a map in front of you with little letters on it. If that could be returned. Just as a last administrative exercise, if you could put an X, since we haven't used that letter, and this is the last thing I'm going to ask you to mark on the map, if you can put an X on the spot where Onofrius fountain is to be found.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Zarkovica is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If you could perhaps -- yes. I can see -- if you could make the X more pronounced, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If I could ask for that map to be tendered into evidence as well as the photograph of Onofrius fountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, that was the plan. The photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes indeed, Your Honour. Maybe just for sake of clarity, if someone could put the fact that this is Mr. Djelo Jusic's map on the map itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: No, the map, the map that's just been handed in. Thank you. I think it's very clear that the map was tendered during the evidence of Mr. Jusic and assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that. Yes, this is the photograph. If that could be assigned also an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P82.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, we're about to conclude your evidence, Mr. Jusic. We've been talking about shells, projectiles, whatever, in the Old Town. Now, I'd like to ask you something about what you actually saw. Did you actually ever see any projectiles with your own eyes, apart from the JNA projectiles? Did you ever see any weapons of any nature apart from what you saw and was captured on your video film?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Of concrete things, I only saw the gunboats that were cruising near Dubrovnik and opening fire, and I saw the shell under the Franciscan cloister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: That was a shell that had landed.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, the one which had landed and was unexploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Now, inside the Old Town itself, did you ever see any military hardware, weapons, guns of any nature anywhere in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: No, impossible. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Did you ever see any Croatian people in the vicinity of the Old Town or in the Old Town itself with military hardware, guns, weapons of any nature?

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, I went inside the city every day, entering it from the east side. From that side there was no weapons at all. And as for the other side, I had no occasion to see, so I don't know. But if there had been any arms there, I would have heard about it, and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, Mr. Jusic, I have one concluded my examination-in-chief. But perhaps before I do that, I could ask you to sign that map. If you could sign it in the margin there on the side where you -- and put the date underneath it as well.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: What is the date today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: 24th of February.

utterances.speaker: DJELO JUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, I thank you ever so much for your evidence in chief. You will be cross-examined. I'm not sure whether that will start today or not, but I have no further questions for you at this moment in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you'd like to start tomorrow, would you, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we'll forego the three minutes that there are and you can start tomorrow. Mr. Jusic, thank you for your attendance today. I must ask that you return tomorrow morning for the evidence to continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hardly wait, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
